title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — भक्तियोगः
titleEn: The Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 12: The Yoga of Devotion
draftNote: Prepared by the Lectorium pipeline from the vulgate text, with a drafting pass, a reviewing pass and a mechanical gate; a printed-edition collation and audio are still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any verse to report a problem.

Devanagari from Sanskrit Wikisource (भगवद्गीता/भक्तियोगः), collated verse by verse against the GRETIL romanized text based on the BORI critical edition (input Tokunaga, rev. J. Smith); every verse where the two differ carries a note giving the BORI reading, and every correction to the Wikisource text is named in its note. Translations made fresh from the Sanskrit with Monier-Williams (1899), Apte (1890) and Śaṅkara's commentary for the traditional sense; no modern translation consulted.

sentences.t: अर्जुन उवाच
sentences.tr: arjuna uvāca
sentences.l: Arjuna said

morph.gloss: Arjuna, the third Pāṇḍava, the great archer (nom. sg.)

sentences.t:
एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते ।
ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः ॥
sentences.tr:
evam satata-yuktāḥ ye bhaktāḥ tvām paryupāsate |
ye ca api akṣaram avyaktam teṣām ke yoga-vit-tamāḥ ||

morph.gloss: disciplined, yoked, devoted (past participle of yuj; nom. pl. masc., agreeing with bhaktāḥ; -āḥ dropped before the following y-)
to worship, attend upon, serve devotedly (paryupāsate: present middle 3rd pl. 'they worship'; pari + upāsate → paryupāsate, -i + u- → -y u-)
even, also (ca + api → cāpi, a + a → ā)
the imperishable (acc. sg. neut., object of paryupāsate, carried over from line 1; api + akṣaram → apyakṣaram, -i + a- → -y a-)
unmanifest (acc. sg. neut.; akṣaram + avyaktam simply written together, final -m unchanged before the vowel)
superlative suffix '-most, best' (yoga-vit-tama: 'the best knower of yoga', nom. pl. masc.)

sentences.l: Thus ever-disciplined, who devotees attend-upon you; and-who also the-imperishable, the-unmanifest — of-them, who [are] the-best-knowers-of-yoga?
sentences.i: Those devotees who, ever disciplined in this way, worship you, and those who also worship the imperishable, the unmanifest — which of these know yoga best?
sentences.n: Arjuna opens the chapter with the question left hanging since chapter 8: is it better to worship Kṛṣṇa in his personal form, or the impersonal, unmanifest akṣara? The verse is built as a relative-correlative pair, ye ... teṣām, 'those who ... of them' — a construction this chapter uses repeatedly — with the verb paryupāsate, 'they worship, attend upon', supplied in line 1 and understood again in line 2. Sandhi: bhaktās tvāṃ is bhaktāḥ + tvām (-āḥ + t- → -ās t-); cāpy akṣaram is ca + api + akṣaram (ca+api→cāpi, a+a→ā; api+akṣaram→apyakṣaram, -i+a-→-y a-).

sentences.t: श्रीभगवानुवाच
sentences.tr: śrībhagavān uvāca
sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined)

sentences.t:
मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ।
श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥
sentences.tr:
mayi āveśya manaḥ ye mām nitya-yuktāḥ upāsate |
śraddhayā parayā upetāḥ te me yukta-tamāḥ matāḥ ||

morph.gloss: I (mayi: loc. sg. 'in me, on me')
to fix upon, enter (āveśya: gerund 'having fixed'; mayi + āveśya → mayy āveśya, -i + ā- → -y ā-)
mind (acc. sg. neut., object of āveśya; -aḥ before y- → -o)
disciplined (nom. pl. masc.: 'ever-disciplined'; nityayuktāḥ + upāsate → nityayuktā upāsate, -āḥ + u- → -ā-, the visarga simply dropping before a vowel)
to worship, wait upon (upāsate: present middle 3rd pl. 'they worship')
supreme, highest (parayā: instr. sg. fem., agreeing with śraddhayā: 'with supreme faith'; parayā + upetāḥ → parayopetāḥ, -ā + u- → -o-)
to come to possess, approach (upeta: past participle 'endowed with, possessed of', nom. pl. masc.)
they (te: nom. pl. masc.; upetāḥ + te → upetās te, -āḥ + t- → -ās t-)
I (me: enclitic gen. sg. 'by me' (genitive of agent with mataḥ))
superlative suffix (yukta-tama: 'most disciplined', nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before m- → -ā)
to think, hold to be (mata: past participle 'considered, held', nom. pl. masc.)

sentences.l: On-me, having-fixed the-mind, who me constantly-disciplined worship, with faith supreme endowed — they by-me [as] most-disciplined [are] held.
sentences.i: Those who fix their mind on me and worship me, ever disciplined and endowed with supreme faith — these I hold to be the most disciplined.
sentences.n: The Blessed Lord answers Arjuna's question directly, at least for now: those who fix the mind on him personally (mayi āveśya manaḥ) he calls yuktatamāḥ, 'most disciplined' — though the chapter goes on to qualify this at length. Sandhi: mayy āveśya is mayi + āveśya (-i+ā-→-y ā-), a glide-formation pattern that recurs through the chapter whenever mayi meets a following vowel; nityayuktā upāsate shows a final -āḥ simply dropping before a vowel, with no trace and no avagraha (contrast the -aḥ+a-→-o' pattern, reserved for a following short a-); parayopetās te packs parayā+upetāḥ (-ā+u-→-o-) and upetāḥ+te (-āḥ+t-→-ās t-).

sentences.t:
ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते ।
सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् ॥
sentences.tr:
ye tu akṣaram anirdeśyam avyaktam paryupāsate |
sarvatra-gam acintyam ca kūṭastham acalam dhruvam ||

morph.gloss: but, on the other hand (tu + akṣaram → tvakṣaram, -u + a- → -v a-)
the imperishable (acc. sg. neut., object of paryupāsate)
indefinable, that cannot be pointed to (negated gerundive of nir-diś; acc. sg. neut.)
unmanifest (acc. sg. neut.; the three descriptive words simply written joined, final -m unchanged before each following vowel)
to worship, attend upon (paryupāsate: present middle 3rd pl.)
going everywhere, all-pervading (sarvatra 'everywhere' + gam 'go'; acc. sg. neut., agreeing with akṣaram of v.3a)
inconceivable, unthinkable (gerundive of cint, negated; acc. sg. neut.; the two words simply written joined)
standing at the peak, unchanging (kūṭa 'peak, summit' + stha 'standing'; acc. sg. neut.)
unmoving, motionless (acc. sg. neut.; again written joined with no phonetic change)

sentences.l: But-who the-imperishable, the-indefinable, the-unmanifest attend-upon — all-pervading and-inconceivable, and standing-at-the-peak, unmoving, fixed:
sentences.i: But those who instead worship the imperishable, the indefinable, the unmanifest — all-pervading, inconceivable, unchanging, unmoving, eternal —
sentences.n: This completes the second alternative of verse 1's question with a stack of near-synonyms for the impersonal absolute, all agreeing with akṣaram: anirdeśya 'indefinable', avyakta 'unmanifest', sarvatra-ga 'going everywhere', acintya 'inconceivable', kūṭa-stha 'standing unchanging at the peak' (kūṭa properly 'summit', used of what stays fixed while all else moves), acala 'unmoving', dhruva 'constant'. The verse and the next form one sentence; the main verb, te prāpnuvanti, comes only in verse 4. Sandhi: tv akṣaram is tu + akṣaram (-u+a-→-v a-, the first instance in this chapter of u fusing to a glide before a vowel); sarvatragam acintyaṃ and kūṭastham acalaṃ are simply pairs of words written joined, the final -m unchanged before the vowel that follows — the same convention already seen at verse 1's akṣaram avyaktam.

sentences.t:
संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः ।
ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
sentences.tr:
saṃniyamya indriya-grāmam sarvatra sama-buddhayaḥ |
te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ ||

morph.gloss: to restrain fully, curb (saṃniyamya: gerund 'having fully restrained'; saṃniyamya + indriya → saṃniyamyendriya, -a + i- → -e-)
multitude, collection (indriya-grāma: 'the whole array of senses', acc. sg., object of saṃniyamya)
to attain, reach (prāpnuvanti: present 3rd pl. 'they attain')
alone, only (mām + eva simply written joined, no phonetic change)
welfare, good (sarva-bhūta-hita: 'the welfare of all beings', loc. sg.)
to delight in, be devoted to (rata: past participle 'delighting in, intent on', nom. pl. masc.)

sentences.l: Having-fully-restrained the-whole-array-of-the-senses, everywhere even-minded, they attain me alone, in-the-welfare-of-all-beings delighting.
sentences.i: Restraining the whole array of the senses, even-minded everywhere and delighting in the welfare of all beings, they attain me alone.
sentences.n: The sentence begun in verse 3 concludes on the poem's recurring reassurance (cf. 6.31, 9.29) that the personal and impersonal paths arrive at the very same goal: te prāpnuvanti mām eva, 'they attain me, and none other'. Saṃniyamyendriyagrāmam and sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ describe the akṣara-worshippers' discipline, in effect a portrait matching the bhaktas described in verses 6-7. Sandhi: saṃniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ is saṃniyamya + indriya-grāmam (-a+i-→-e-); māmeva is mām + eva, simply written together with no phonetic change.

sentences.t:
क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् ।
अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
kleśaḥ adhikataraḥ teṣām avyakta-āsakta-cetasām |
avyaktā hi gatiḥ duḥkham dehavadbhiḥ avāpyate ||

morph.gloss: greater (comparative of adhika 'more'; nom. sg., predicate; kleśaḥ + adhikataraḥ → kleśo'dhikataraḥ, -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
they (teṣām: gen. pl. 'for them'; adhikataraḥ + teṣām → adhikatarasteṣām, -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
unmanifest (first compound member; avyakta + āsakta → avyaktāsakta, -a + ā- → -ā-)
attached, clinging (past participle of ā-sañj, second compound member)
mind (avyakta-āsakta-cetas: 'whose mind is attached to the unmanifest', gen. pl. bahuvrīhi, agreeing with teṣām)
unmanifest (avyaktā: nom. sg. fem., agreeing with gatiḥ)
path, course, goal (nom. sg. fem., subject of avāpyate; -iḥ + d- → -ir d-)
pain, difficulty (acc. sg. neut., used adverbially: 'with difficulty, painfully')
embodied, possessing a body (instr. pl. 'by embodied beings'; dehavadbhiḥ + avāpyate → dehavadbhir avāpyate, -iḥ + a- → -ir a-)
to attain, reach (avāpyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is attained')

sentences.l: Trouble greater [is] for-them whose-minds-are-attached-to-the-unmanifest; the-unmanifest indeed [as] a-goal, with-difficulty, by-embodied-beings is-attained.
sentences.i: For those whose minds cling to the unmanifest, the trouble is greater; the unmanifest goal is reached only with difficulty by those who live in a body.
sentences.n: Having shown that both paths reach the same end, Kṛṣṇa now weighs their difficulty and finds the impersonal one harder: kleśaḥ adhikataraḥ, 'the trouble is greater', for avyaktāsakta-cetasām, 'those whose minds are fixed on the unmanifest' — not wrong, only harder for an embodied being (deha-vat, 'possessing a body') to sustain, since it gives the mind no form to hold onto. This sets up the easier path urged from verse 6 on. The whole first line is written as one unbroken string: kleśo'dhikatarasteṣāmavyaktāsaktacetasām packs kleśaḥ+adhikataraḥ (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha), adhikataraḥ+teṣām (-aḥ+t-→-as t-), and avyakta+āsakta fusing inside the compound (-a+ā-→-ā-). Gatir duḥkhaṃ and dehavadbhir avāpyate both show a final -iḥ becoming -ir before the next word.

sentences.t:
ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः ।
अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥
sentences.tr:
ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya mat-parāḥ |
ananyena eva yogena mām dhyāyantaḥ upāsate ||

morph.gloss: I (mayi: loc. sg. 'in me, on me')
to lay down, entrust, deposit (saṃnyasya: gerund 'having laid down, having entrusted')
me, my (stem form of aham in compounds; first member)
intent on, having as one's highest aim (mat-para: nom. pl. masc.)
to meditate (dhyāyantaḥ: present participle, nom. pl. masc. 'meditating'; final -ḥ dropped before the vowel u- of upāsate)

sentences.l: But-who all actions in-me having-entrusted, intent-on-me, by-undivided yoga alone meditating, worship [me]:
sentences.i: But those who entrust all their actions to me, intent on me as their highest goal, and, meditating on me with undivided yoga, worship me —
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa now describes the easier, personal path: karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya, 'having laid down all actions in me' (anticipating the surrender taught in chapter 18), mat-parāḥ, 'intent on me', dhyāyantaḥ upāsate, 'meditating, they worship' — a chain of descriptions completed only in verse 7's promise. Ananyena eva yogena, 'by undivided yoga alone', is the poem's constant insistence on singleness of devotion (cf. ananya-cetāḥ at 8.14). Sandhi: ananyenaiva is ananyena + eva (-a+e-→-ai-); dhyāyanta upāsate shows the final -aḥ of the participle silently dropping before the vowel u- — the first clear instance in this chapter of the pattern already at work, unmarked, in verse 2's nityayuktā.

sentences.t:
तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् ।
भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥
sentences.tr:
teṣām aham samuddhartā mṛtyu-saṃsāra-sāgarāt |
bhavāmi na cirāt pārtha mayi āveśita-cetasām ||

morph.gloss: they (teṣām: gen. pl. 'of them, for them')
to lift up, rescue, deliver (samuddhartā: nom. sg. agent noun 'deliverer, rescuer')
the cycle of rebirth, transmigration (second compound member)
ocean, sea (mṛtyu-saṃsāra-sāgara: 'the ocean of death and transmigration', abl. sg. 'from the ocean of')
to be, become (bhavāmi: present 1st sg. 'I become')
not (with cirāt: 'not [after] a long time', i.e. soon)
I (mayi: loc. sg. 'in me'; mayi + āveśita → mayy āveśita, -i + ā- → -y ā-)
to fix, enter (āveśita: causative past participle 'made to enter, fixed')
mind (āveśita-cetasām: 'of those whose minds are fixed [on me]', gen. pl. bahuvrīhi, in apposition to teṣām of line 1)

sentences.l: Of-them I [am] the-deliverer from-the-ocean-of-death-and-transmigration, I become before-long, O son of Pṛthā, of-those-whose-minds-are-fixed-on-me.
sentences.i: For them I quickly become the deliverer from the ocean of death and rebirth, Pārtha — for those whose minds are fixed on me.
sentences.n: The promised result of verse 6: Kṛṣṇa himself becomes their samuddhartā, 'rescuer', from mṛtyu-saṃsāra-sāgarāt, 'the ocean of death and transmigration' — one of the poem's several ocean-of-saṃsāra images (cf. 4.36's jñāna-plava, 'raft of knowledge'). Na cirāt, 'not after a long time', i.e. soon, deliberately answers verse 5's warning that the impersonal path is slow. Pārtha, 'son of Pṛthā' (Kuntī), addresses Arjuna. Sandhi: mayy āveśita- is mayi + āveśita (-i+ā-→-y ā-), the glide pattern already seen at verse 2's mayy āveśya.

sentences.t:
मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय ।
निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥
sentences.tr:
mayi eva manaḥ ādhatsva mayi buddhim niveśaya |
nivasiṣyasi mayi eva ataḥ ūrdhvam na saṃśayaḥ ||

morph.gloss: alone, only (mayi + eva → mayy eva, -i + e- → -y e-)
mind (acc. sg. neut., object of ādhatsva; -aḥ dropped before the vowel ā- of ādhatsva)
to place, fix upon (ādhatsva: imperative middle 2nd sg. 'fix!')
to settle, fix (niveśaya: causative imperative 2nd sg. 'fix! settle!')
to dwell (nivasiṣyasi: future 2nd sg. 'you will dwell')
alone (mayi + eva → mayy eva, as above)
from this, thereafter (ataḥ: -aḥ dropped before the vowel ū- of ūrdhvam)

sentences.l: On-me alone the-mind fix, in-me the-understanding place; you-will-dwell in-me alone thereafter — no doubt.
sentences.i: Fix your mind on me alone, place your understanding in me; from then on you will dwell in me alone — of this there is no doubt.
sentences.n: Two parallel imperatives, ādhatsva and niveśaya, open the practical instruction that runs through verse 12, moving from this hardest ideal (mind wholly fixed on Kṛṣṇa) down through progressively easier alternatives for one who cannot manage it. Mayy eva, 'in me alone', frames both halves of the verse; ataḥ ūrdhvam, 'from this point on', means after death. Sandhi: mana ādhatsva shows the same silent visarga-drop before a vowel as verse 6's dhyāyanta upāsate, here before ā- rather than u-; mayy eva is mayi + eva (-i+e-→-y e-); ata ūrdhvam again drops its visarga silently, this time before ū-.

sentences.t:
अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् ।
अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनंजय ॥
sentences.tr:
atha cittam samādhātum na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram |
abhyāsa-yogena tataḥ mām iccha āptum dhanaṃjaya ||

morph.gloss: to fix firmly, concentrate (samādhātum: infinitive 'to fix firmly')
to be able (śaknoṣi: present 2nd sg. 'you are able')
steady, firm (acc. sg. neut., predicate with cittam)
yoga, discipline (abhyāsa-yoga: 'the discipline of practice', instr. sg.)
then, in that case (-aḥ before m- → -o)
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me', object of āptum)
to wish, desire (iccha: imperative 2nd sg. 'desire!'; iccha + āptum → icchāptum, -a + ā- → -ā-)
'winner of wealth', an epithet of Arjuna (vocative)

sentences.l: But-if the-mind to-fix-firmly you-are-not-able, steadily, on-me — then, by-the-yoga-of-practice, desire to-attain me, O Winner-of-wealth.
sentences.i: But if you cannot steady your mind firmly on me, then seek to reach me through the yoga of repeated practice, Dhanaṃjaya.
sentences.n: The first step down from verse 8's ideal: if the mind cannot be held motionless on Kṛṣṇa (samādhātum ... sthiram), the next resort is abhyāsa-yoga, 'the yoga of repeated practice' — patient, habitual effort rather than achieved stillness. Icchāptum packs iccha, the imperative of iṣ 'to wish' ('desire!'), with the infinitive āptum 'to attain' (-a+ā-→-ā-): 'desire to attain [me]'. Dhanaṃjaya, 'winner of wealth' (won in the plunder of conquered kings), is a recurring epithet of Arjuna (cf. 1.15, 4.41, 7.7, 9.9). Sandhi: tato is tataḥ, -aḥ before m- → -o.

sentences.t:
अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव ।
मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन्सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥
sentences.tr:
abhyāse api asamarthaḥ asi mat-karma-paramaḥ bhava |
mad-artham api karmāṇi kurvan siddhim avāpsyasi ||

morph.gloss: practice (loc. sg. 'in practice'; abhyāse + api → abhyāse'pi, -e + a- → -e ' with avagraha)
incapable, unable (nom. sg., predicate; asamarthaḥ + asi → asamartho'si, -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
supreme, having as one's highest aim (mat-karma-parama: nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ before bh- → -o)
sake, purpose (mad-artham: adverbial acc. 'for my sake')
to do, perform (kurvan: present participle, nom. sg. masc. 'doing, performing')
to attain, obtain (avāpsyasi: future 2nd sg. 'you will attain')

sentences.l: If-in-practice too incapable you-are, be one-for-whom-action-for-me-is-supreme; for-my-sake even actions performing, perfection you-will-attain.
sentences.i: If you are unable even for that practice, be intent on action done for my sake; performing actions for my sake, you will attain perfection.
sentences.n: A second step down: if even abhyāsa-yoga is out of reach, the instruction becomes mat-karma-paramaḥ bhava, 'be one for whom action done for me is supreme' — ordinary karma-yoga redirected toward Kṛṣṇa, the same teaching found in chapters 3 and 9. Mad-artham api karmāṇi kurvan, 'even performing actions for my sake', promises siddhim, 'success, accomplishment' — the same word chapter 18 uses technically for the goal of disciplined action. Sandhi: the first line strings three visarga-elisions together — abhyāse'py asamartho'si packs abhyāse+api (-e+a-→-e' with avagraha), api+asamarthaḥ (-i+a-→-y a-), and asamarthaḥ+asi (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); mat-karma-paramo is mat-karma-paramaḥ, -aḥ before bh- → -o.

sentences.t:
अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः ।
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥
sentences.tr:
atha etat api aśaktaḥ asi kartum mad-yogam āśritaḥ |
sarva-karma-phala-tyāgam tataḥ kuru yata-ātmavān ||

morph.gloss: then, but if (atha + etat → athaitat, -a + e- → -ai-)
this (etat: acc. sg. neut., referring to the practice just prescribed; etat + api → etadapi, -t + a- → -d a-)
unable, incapable (nom. sg., predicate; aśaktaḥ + asi → aśakto'si, -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
yoga, discipline (mad-yogam: 'discipline directed toward me', acc. sg., object of āśritaḥ)
to resort to, take refuge in (āśrita: past participle 'relying on', nom. sg.)
relinquishment (sarva-karma-phala-tyāga: 'the relinquishment of the fruit of all action', acc. sg.)
controlled, restrained (past participle of yam, first member)

sentences.l: But-if this too you-are-unable to-do, resorting-to-my-yoga, then the-relinquishment-of-the-fruit-of-all-action do, self-controlled.
sentences.i: And if you cannot manage even this, resorting to the yoga directed toward me, then give up the fruit of all action, with your self mastered.
sentences.n: The third and last step down before verse 12's summary ranking: mad-yogam āśritaḥ, 'taking refuge in yoga directed toward me' (still oriented to Kṛṣṇa, unlike ordinary renunciation), give up sarva-karma-phala-tyāgam, 'the fruit of all action' — the very teaching of 2.47, offered here as the fallback for one who cannot even perform action as an offering. Yata-ātmavān, 'self-controlled', echoes the self-mastery demanded throughout the chapter. Sandhi: athaitad apy aśakto'si is the densest line so far, packing atha+etat (-a+e-→-ai-), etat+api (-t+a-→-d a-), api+aśaktaḥ (-i+a-→-y a-), and aśaktaḥ+asi (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha) into one breath.

sentences.t:
श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते ।
ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् ॥
sentences.tr:
śreyaḥ hi jñānam abhyāsāt jñānāt dhyānam viśiṣyate |
dhyānāt karma-phala-tyāgaḥ tyāgāt śāntiḥ anantaram ||

morph.gloss: better, preferable (nom. sg. neut., predicate; -aḥ before h- → -o)
practice, mechanical repetition (abl. sg. 'than practice', ablative of comparison)
knowledge (jñānāt: abl. sg. 'than knowledge'; abhyāsāt + jñānāt → abhyāsāj jñānāt, -t + j- → -j j-)
meditation (nom. sg. neut., subject of viśiṣyate; jñānāt + dhyānam → jñānād dhyānam, -t + dh- → -d dh-)
to excel, be superior (viśiṣyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is distinguished, is superior')
relinquishment (karma-phala-tyāga: nom. sg., subject; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
relinquishment (tyāgāt: abl. sg. 'from relinquishment'; tyāgāt + śāntiḥ → tyāgācchāntiḥ, -t + ś- → -c ch-)

sentences.l: Better indeed [is] knowledge than-practice; than-knowledge meditation is-superior; than-meditation the-relinquishment-of-the-fruit-of-action; from-relinquishment peace immediately-follows.
sentences.i: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is superior to knowledge; better than meditation is giving up the fruit of action; from that giving-up, peace follows at once.
sentences.n: A ranked ladder packed into a single verse, each stage bettering the last: abhyāsa (mechanical practice) < jñāna (knowledge) < dhyāna (meditation) < karma-phala-tyāga (relinquishing the fruit of action) → śānti (peace), reached anantaram, 'immediately'. This is not a contradiction of the descending steps of verses 8-11 but their summary read from the top down. Sandhi runs through both lines: abhyāsāj jñānāt is abhyāsāt+jñānāt (-t+j-→-j j-); jñānād dhyānaṃ is jñānāt+dhyānam (-t+dh-→-d dh-); tyāgas tyāgāt is tyāgaḥ+tyāgāt (-aḥ+t-→-as t-); tyāgācchāntir is tyāgāt+śāntiḥ (-t+ś-→-c ch-, a new assimilation, not yet seen this chapter), followed by the now-familiar -iḥ+a-→-ir a- before anantaram.

sentences.t:
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च ।
निर्ममो निरहंकारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥
sentences.tr:
adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānām maitraḥ karuṇaḥ eva ca |
nirmamaḥ nirahaṃkāraḥ sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ kṣamī ||

morph.gloss: not hating, free from hatred (a-dveṣṭṛ: 'non-hater', nom. sg. agent noun)
being, creature (sarva-bhūta: gen. pl. 'of all beings')
compassionate (nom. sg.; -aḥ dropped before the vowel e- of eva)
free from possessiveness, without 'mine' (nom. sg.; -aḥ before n- → -o)
free from egoism, without self-assertion (nom. sg. masc.)
pleasure (sama-duḥkha-sukha: 'the same in pain and pleasure', nom. sg.)

sentences.l: Not-hating of-all-beings, friendly and compassionate, without-'mine', without-egoism, the-same-in-pain-and-pleasure, forbearing;
sentences.i: Free from hatred toward all beings, friendly and compassionate, without possessiveness or egoism, the same in pain and pleasure, forbearing;
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa turns from the ladder of practice to a portrait of the ideal devotee, a string of qualities running through verse 19, each stretch ending in the refrain sa me priyaḥ, 'he is dear to me' (first at v.14). Nirmama and nirahaṃkāra name the twin roots of bondage the poem attacks throughout — 'mine' and 'I' — and sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ recalls the touchstone of equanimity set at 2.15. This whole verse is a string of nominative adjectives describing one still-unnamed subject; the subject's identity (the devotee) and the main verb arrive only in verse 14. Sandhi: karuṇa eva shows the -aḥ silently dropping before the vowel e-, as already seen at verses 8's ata ūrdhvam; nirmamo is nirmamaḥ, -aḥ before n- → -o.

sentences.t:
संतुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः ।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
sentences.tr:
saṃtuṣṭaḥ satatam yogī yata-ātmā dṛḍha-niścayaḥ |
mayi arpita-manaḥ-buddhiḥ yaḥ mad-bhaktaḥ saḥ me priyaḥ ||

morph.gloss: to be satisfied (saṃtuṣṭa: past participle 'content', nom. sg.)
controlled (past participle of yam, first member)
I (mayi: loc. sg. 'on me'; mayi + arpita → mayy arpita, -i + a- → -y a-)
to fix, offer (arpita: causative past participle 'offered, fixed')
mind (first compound member; manaḥ + buddhi → manobuddhi, -aḥ + b- → -o)
understanding, intellect (mayi-arpita-manaḥ-buddhi: 'whose mind and understanding are fixed on me', nom. sg. bahuvrīhi, agreeing with yaḥ; buddhiḥ + yaḥ → buddhir yaḥ, -iḥ + y- → -ir y-)

sentences.l: Content, constantly, the-disciplined-one, self-controlled, of-firm-resolve, whose-mind-and-understanding-are-fixed-on-me — who my-devotee [is], he to-me [is] dear.
sentences.i: Content, always disciplined, self-controlled, of firm resolve, mind and understanding fixed on me — whoever is my devotee in this way is dear to me.
sentences.n: The list from verse 13 continues and the first refrain arrives: yo mad-bhaktaḥ, sa me priyaḥ, 'whoever is my devotee, he is dear to me' — the frame (yaḥ ... saḥ) that shapes verses 14-17, this exact refrain (with small variations) closing verses 14, 16 and 17; verses 18-19 continue the devotee-portrait without repeating the frame, resolving instead at verse 19's naraḥ, and the whole sequence returns, intensified, at 19-20. Mayy arpita-manaḥ-buddhiḥ, 'whose mind and understanding are offered up in me', gives bhakti concrete content here: not feeling alone but the placing of the inner faculties themselves in Kṛṣṇa. Sandhi: mayy arpita- is mayi + arpita (-i+a-→-y a-); manobuddhir yo packs manaḥ+buddhiḥ (-aḥ+b-→-o) and buddhiḥ+yaḥ (-iḥ+y-→-ir y-).

sentences.t:
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः ।
हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥
sentences.tr:
yasmāt na udvijate lokaḥ lokāt na udvijate ca yaḥ |
harṣa-amarṣa-bhaya-udvegaiḥ muktaḥ yaḥ saḥ ca me priyaḥ ||

morph.gloss: who (yasmāt: abl. sg. 'from whom, because of whom')
to be disturbed, shrink away (udvijate: present middle 3rd sg. 'is disturbed'; na + udvijate → nodvijate, -a + u- → -o-)
the world, people (nom. sg.; -aḥ before l- → -o)
the world (abl. sg. 'from the world'; lokāt + na → lokānna, -t + n- → -n n-)
to be disturbed, shrink away (udvijate: present middle 3rd sg.; na + udvijate → nodvijate, as above)
joy, elation (first compound member; harṣa + amarṣa → harṣāmarṣa, -a + a- → -ā-)
fear (third compound member; bhaya + udvega → bhayodvega, -a + u- → -o-)
agitation, anxiety (harṣa-amarṣa-bhaya-udvega: instr. pl.; udvegaiḥ + muktaḥ → udvegair muktaḥ, -aiḥ + m- → -air m-)
to release (mukta: past participle 'freed', nom. sg.; muktaḥ + yaḥ → mukto yaḥ, -aḥ before y- → -o)

sentences.l: From-whom not-is-disturbed the-world, and-who from-the-world is-not-disturbed, and-who by-joy-resentment-fear-and-agitation [is] freed — he too to-me [is] dear.
sentences.i: He from whom the world does not shrink, and who does not shrink from the world, and who is free of elation, resentment, fear and anxiety — he too is dear to me.
sentences.n: A mutual, reciprocal ease with the world — yasmāt na udvijate lokaḥ, 'the world is not disturbed by him', lokāt na udvijate ca yaḥ, 'and he is not disturbed by the world' — followed by freedom from the four ordinary agitations: harṣa (elation), amarṣa (impatience or resentment), bhaya (fear), udvega (anxiety). Sandhi: yasmānnodvijate and lokānnodvijate both show -t+n-→-n n- followed by na+udvijate fusing to nodvijate (-a+u-→-o-, the same fusion twice); harṣāmarṣabhayodvegair muktaḥ strings two vowel-fusions inside the dvandva compound (-a+a-→-ā-, -a+u-→-o-) before the instrumental plural's visarga elides before m- (-aiḥ+m-→-air m-); mukto yaḥ shows the familiar -aḥ before y- → -o.

sentences.t:
अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः ।
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
sentences.tr:
anapekṣaḥ śuciḥ dakṣaḥ udāsīnaḥ gata-vyathaḥ |
sarva-ārambha-parityāgī yaḥ mad-bhaktaḥ saḥ me priyaḥ ||

morph.gloss: without expectation, indifferent to results (nom. sg.)
pure (nom. sg.; śuciḥ + dakṣaḥ → śucir dakṣaḥ, -iḥ + d- → -ir d-)
skillful, capable (nom. sg.; -aḥ dropped before the vowel u- of udāsīnaḥ)
indifferent, unconcerned, neutral (nom. sg.; -aḥ before g- → -o)
gone, departed (past participle of gam, first member)
anguish, distress (gata-vyatha: 'free of distress', nom. sg.)
all (first member; sarva + ārambha → sarvārambha, -a + ā- → -ā-)
one who relinquishes, renounces (sarva-ārambha-parityāgin: 'one who has given up every undertaking', nom. sg.)

sentences.l: Without-expectation, pure, capable, indifferent, free-from-distress, one-who-has-relinquished-every-undertaking — who my-devotee [is], he to-me [is] dear.
sentences.i: Free from expectation, pure, capable, unconcerned, past all distress, having given up every selfish undertaking — whoever is my devotee like this is dear to me.
sentences.n: The list resumes and the refrain repeats. Sarva-ārambha-parityāgī, 'one who has given up every undertaking', does not contradict the poem's earlier insistence on continued action (ch.3): the tradition reads ārambha here as self-interested new projects, not all activity as such. Sandhi: śucir dakṣa udāsīno strings three words together — śuciḥ+dakṣaḥ (-iḥ+d-→-ir d-), dakṣaḥ silently losing its visarga before the vowel u- (as at verse 6's dhyāyanta upāsate), and udāsīnaḥ+gata- (-aḥ before g- → -o); sarvārambha- is sarva+ārambha (-a+ā-→-ā-); yo mad-bhaktaḥ is yaḥ+mad-bhaktaḥ, -aḥ before m- → -o.

sentences.t:
यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥
sentences.tr:
yaḥ na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
śubha-aśubha-parityāgī bhaktimān yaḥ saḥ me priyaḥ ||

morph.gloss: to rejoice, be elated (hṛṣyati: present 3rd sg.)
to desire, long for (kāṅkṣati: present 3rd sg.)
good, auspicious (first member; śubha + aśubha → śubhāśubha, -a + a- → -ā-)
one who relinquishes (śubha-aśubha-parityāgin: 'one who has given up [attachment to] both good and bad', nom. sg.)
devoted, possessing devotion (bhaktimān: nom. sg. masc.)
who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative; bhaktimān + yaḥ simply written joined)

sentences.l: Who not rejoices, not hates, not grieves, not desires, one-who-has-relinquished-both-good-and-bad — who [has] devotion, he to-me [is] dear.
sentences.i: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor desires, who has let go of both good and bad fortune alike — whoever has such devotion is dear to me.
sentences.n: A verse of four flat negations (na hṛṣyati, na dveṣṭi, na śocati, na kāṅkṣati) describing equanimity toward whatever comes, followed by śubhāśubha-parityāgī, 'one who has renounced [attachment to] both good and bad' (echoing 2.38's samaḥ labhālabhau). This is the chapter's first bare use of bhaktimān, 'possessing bhakti, devoted' — bhakti itself, translated throughout this chapter (as since chapters 7 and 9) as 'devotion', now appearing on its own rather than only inside the compound mad-bhaktaḥ. Sandhi: yo na is yaḥ+na, -aḥ before n- → -o; śubhāśubha- is śubha+aśubha, -a+a-→-ā-.

sentences.t:
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः ।
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥
sentences.tr:
samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā māna-apamānayoḥ |
śīta-uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅga-vivarjitaḥ ||

morph.gloss: dishonor, disrespect (māna-apamāna: 'honor and dishonor', loc. dual; māna + apamāna → mānāpamāna, -a + a- → -ā-)
heat (second member; śīta + uṣṇa → śītoṣṇa, -a + u- → -o-)
devoid of, free from (past participle of vi-vṛj, nom. sg.)

sentences.l: The-same toward-an-enemy and toward-a-friend, likewise in-honor-and-dishonor; in-cold-and-heat, pleasure-and-pain, the-same, free-from-attachment;
sentences.i: The same toward enemy and friend, and likewise in honor and dishonor; the same in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, free from attachment;
sentences.n: The chapter's one real vulgate/BORI variant falls here: this text reads mānāpamānayoḥ, 'in honor and dishonor' (apamāna), while the BORI critical edition reads mānāvamānayoḥ, 'in honor and disrespect' (avamāna, a near-synonym also meaning 'dishonor, disrespect'); the sense is essentially unchanged, and the vulgate reading is what is translated here. The verse continues the equanimity-list toward opposite pairs — enemy/friend, honor/dishonor, cold/heat, pleasure/pain — the standard set the poem returns to at 2.14-15, 6.7 and 14.24-25. Sandhi: mānāpamānayoḥ is māna+apamānayoḥ (-a+a-→-ā-); śītoṣṇa- is śīta+uṣṇa (-a+u-→-o-).

sentences.t:
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येन केनचित् ।
अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥
sentences.tr:
tulya-nindā-stutiḥ maunī santuṣṭaḥ yena kenacit |
aniketaḥ sthira-matiḥ bhaktimān me priyaḥ naraḥ ||

morph.gloss: praise (tulya-nindā-stuti: 'one to whom blame and praise are alike', nom. sg. bahuvrīhi; stutiḥ + maunī → stutir maunī, -iḥ + m- → -ir m-)
silent, taciturn, a man of few words (nom. sg.)
to be satisfied (santuṣṭa: past participle 'content', nom. sg.; -aḥ before y- → -o)
anything at all (kena-cit: instr. sg.; yena kenacit: idiomatic 'with whatever comes')
without a fixed abode, homeless (nom. sg.)
mind, thought (sthira-mati: 'steady-minded', nom. sg.; -iḥ + bh- → -ir bh-)
devoted, possessing devotion (bhaktimān: nom. sg. masc.)
I (me: enclitic gen. sg. 'to me'; bhaktimān + me simply written joined)

sentences.l: To-whom-blame-and-praise-are-equal, silent, content with-whatever [comes], homeless, steady-minded, devoted — to-me dear [is that] man.
sentences.i: Indifferent to blame and praise, silent, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady-minded and devoted — such a man is dear to me.
sentences.n: The last of the devotee-portraits before the summary of verse 20, and the first to name its subject openly as naraḥ, 'the man', rather than leaving him to a bare relative pronoun. Yena kenacit santuṣṭaḥ, 'content with whatever, by whatever [comes]', is an idiom for contentment regardless of circumstance; aniketaḥ, 'without a fixed dwelling', suggests the wandering ascetic's detachment from possessions more than literal homelessness. Sandhi: stutir maunī is stutiḥ+maunī (-iḥ+m-→-ir m-); santuṣṭo is santuṣṭaḥ, -aḥ before y- → -o; sthiramatir bhaktimān is sthiramatiḥ+bhaktimān (-iḥ+bh-→-ir bh-); priyo naraḥ is priyaḥ+naraḥ, -aḥ before n- → -o.

sentences.t:
ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते ।
श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः ॥
sentences.tr:
ye tu dharmya-amṛtam idam yathā-uktam paryupāsate |
śraddadhānāḥ mat-paramāḥ bhaktāḥ te atīva me priyāḥ ||

morph.gloss: righteous, in accord with dharma (first member; dharmya + amṛta → dharmyāmṛta, -a + a- → -ā-)
nectar, ambrosia, the deathless (dharmya-amṛta: 'this nectar of dharma', acc. sg. neut.)
this (idam: acc. sg. neut., in apposition)
as, according to (first compound member; yathā + uktam → yathoktam, -ā + u- → -o-)
to speak (ukta: past participle 'spoken, said'; yathā-ukta: 'as has been said', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with idam)
to worship, attend upon (present middle 3rd pl.)
to have faith, believe (śraddadhāna: present middle participle 'having faith', nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before m- → -ā)
supreme, highest (mat-parama: 'having me as their highest goal', nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before bh- → -ā)
devotee (nom. pl. masc.; bhaktāḥ + te → bhaktās te, -āḥ + t- → -ās t-)
they (te: nom. pl. masc.; te + atīva → te'tīva, -e + a- → -e ' with avagraha)

sentences.l: But-who this nectar-of-dharma, as-has-been-said, attend-upon, having-faith, having-me-as-their-highest-goal — those devotees exceedingly to-me [are] dear.
sentences.i: But those who, full of faith, attend on this nectar of dharma as it has been taught, holding me as their highest goal — such devotees are exceedingly dear to me.
sentences.n: The chapter's closing summary gathers everything into one sentence and ends on its key word, priyāḥ, 'dear' — echoing and outdoing the refrain of verses 14-19 (there merely priyaḥ, 'dear', now atīva priyāḥ, 'exceedingly dear'). Dharmyāmṛtam idam, 'this nectar in accord with dharma', names the whole preceding teaching (yathā uktam, 'as it has been stated') as a kind of ambrosia — an image the poem uses elsewhere for a teaching that grants freedom from death. Sandhi: dharmyāmṛtam is dharmya+amṛtam (-a+a-→-ā-); yathoktaṃ is yathā+uktam (-ā+u-→-o-); bhaktās te'tīva packs bhaktāḥ+te (-āḥ+t-→-ās t-) and te+atīva (-e+a-→-e' with avagraha).

glossary.अर्जुन: arjunaḥ — Arjuna — Arjuna, the third Pāṇḍava, the great archer (nom. sg.)
glossary.उवाच: uvāca — vac — to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')
glossary.एवं: evam — evam — thus, in this way (adverb)
glossary.सततयुक्ता: satata-yuktāḥ — satata — constant, always (first compound member); yukta — disciplined, yoked, devoted (past participle of yuj; nom. pl. masc., agreeing with bhaktāḥ; -āḥ dropped before the following y-)
glossary.ये: ye — yad — who (ye: nom. pl. masc. relative)
glossary.भक्तास्त्वां: bhaktāḥ tvām — bhakta — devotee (nom. pl. masc.); tvam — you (tvām: acc. sg.; -āḥ + t- → -ās t-)
glossary.पर्युपासते: paryupāsate — pari-upa-ās — to worship, attend upon, serve devotedly (paryupāsate: present middle 3rd pl. 'they worship'; pari + upāsate → paryupāsate, -i + u- → -y u-)
glossary.चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं: ca api akṣaram avyaktam — ca — and; api — even, also (ca + api → cāpi, a + a → ā); akṣara — the imperishable (acc. sg. neut., object of paryupāsate, carried over from line 1; api + akṣaram → apyakṣaram, -i + a- → -y a-); avyakta — unmanifest (acc. sg. neut.; akṣaram + avyaktam simply written together, final -m unchanged before the vowel)
glossary.तेषां: teṣām — tad — that, they (teṣām: gen. pl. 'of them')
glossary.के: ke — kim — who? which? (ke: nom. pl. masc.)
glossary.योगवित्तमाः: yoga-vit-tamāḥ — yoga — yoga, discipline (first compound member); vid — to know (vit-, 'knower', second compound member); tama — superlative suffix '-most, best' (yoga-vit-tama: 'the best knower of yoga', nom. pl. masc.)
glossary.श्रीभगवानुवाच: śrī-bhagavān uvāca — śrī — holy, glorious (honorific prefix); bhagavat — the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined); vac — to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')

glossary.शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु: śīta-uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu — śīta — cold (first member); uṣṇa — heat (second member; śīta + uṣṇa → śītoṣṇa, -a + u- → -o-); sukha — pleasure (third member); duḥkha — pain (śīta-uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha: loc. pl.)
glossary.सङ्गविवर्जितः: saṅga-vivarjitaḥ — saṅga — attachment, clinging (first member); vi-varjita — devoid of, free from (past participle of vi-vṛj, nom. sg.)
glossary.तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी: tulya-nindā-stutiḥ maunī — tulya — equal, the same (first compound member); nindā — blame, censure (second compound member); stuti — praise (tulya-nindā-stuti: 'one to whom blame and praise are alike', nom. sg. bahuvrīhi; stutiḥ + maunī → stutir maunī, -iḥ + m- → -ir m-); maunin — silent, taciturn, a man of few words (nom. sg.)
glossary.सन्तुष्टो: santuṣṭaḥ — sam-tuṣ — to be satisfied (santuṣṭa: past participle 'content', nom. sg.; -aḥ before y- → -o)
glossary.येन: yena — yad — who, whatever (yena: instr. sg. neut.)
glossary.केनचित्: kenacit — kim-cit — anything at all (kena-cit: instr. sg.; yena kenacit: idiomatic 'with whatever comes')
glossary.अनिकेतः: aniketaḥ — a-niketa — without a fixed abode, homeless (nom. sg.)
glossary.स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे: sthira-matiḥ bhaktimān me — sthira — steady, firm (first member); mati — mind, thought (sthira-mati: 'steady-minded', nom. sg.; -iḥ + bh- → -ir bh-); bhaktimat — devoted, possessing devotion (bhaktimān: nom. sg. masc.); aham — I (me: enclitic gen. sg. 'to me'; bhaktimān + me simply written joined)
glossary.प्रियो: priyaḥ — priya — dear (nom. sg.; -aḥ before n- → -o)
glossary.नरः: naraḥ — nara — man, person (nom. sg., subject: 'the man')
glossary.धर्म्यामृतमिदं: dharmya-amṛtam idam — dharmya — righteous, in accord with dharma (first member; dharmya + amṛta → dharmyāmṛta, -a + a- → -ā-); amṛta — nectar, ambrosia, the deathless (dharmya-amṛta: 'this nectar of dharma', acc. sg. neut.); idam — this (idam: acc. sg. neut., in apposition)
glossary.यथोक्तं: yathā-uktam — yathā — as, according to (first compound member; yathā + uktam → yathoktam, -ā + u- → -o-); vac — to speak (ukta: past participle 'spoken, said'; yathā-ukta: 'as has been said', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with idam)
glossary.श्रद्दधाना: śraddadhānāḥ — śrad-dhā — to have faith, believe (śraddadhāna: present middle participle 'having faith', nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before m- → -ā)
glossary.मत्परमा: mat-paramāḥ — mad — me (stem form, first member); parama — supreme, highest (mat-parama: 'having me as their highest goal', nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ before bh- → -ā)
glossary.भक्तास्तेऽतीव: bhaktāḥ te atīva — bhakta — devotee (nom. pl. masc.; bhaktāḥ + te → bhaktās te, -āḥ + t- → -ās t-); tad — they (te: nom. pl. masc.; te + atīva → te'tīva, -e + a- → -e ' with avagraha); atīva — exceedingly, very much (adverb)
glossary.प्रियाः: priyāḥ — priya — dear (nom. pl. masc., predicate)

about: Chapter 12, the Yoga of Devotion (Bhaktiyoga), is the poem's short, direct answer to a question left open since chapter 8: is it better to worship Kṛṣṇa in his manifest, personal form, or to meditate on the unmanifest, imperishable absolute beyond all form? Kṛṣṇa answers that both paths reach him, but that fixing the mind on him personally is easier and safer for an embodied being, since the impersonal path is far harder to sustain without a form to hold onto. He then sketches a ladder of practice for those who cannot yet hold their mind steady on him — repeated disciplined practice, then action performed for his sake, then simply relinquishing the fruit of one's action — each step a workable substitute for the one above it, with knowledge, meditation, and renunciation ranked in ascending order toward the peace that renunciation brings. The chapter closes with its best-known passage, a cumulative portrait of the ideal devotee: free of hatred and possessiveness, equable in pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor, praise and blame, undisturbed by the world and undisturbing to it, content with whatever comes, and devoted — a portrait repeated across several verses, each closing on the same refrain, that such a devotee is dear to Kṛṣṇa, culminating in the declaration that those who approach him with faith in this way are supremely dear to him.
